title: Bring the sales lake under Terraform
skills: terraform import or an import block

ticket.subject: Sales lake: stop clicking in the portal
body: I created `rg-saleslake-dev` by hand in the portal last week, with the tags finance needs. Before the pipelines
land in it, I'd like the whole lake described in Terraform (the starter is in `main.tf`, never applied):
- **Keep my resource group.** Terraform must manage it, not delete and recreate it: the budget alert and the
role assignments hang off it. Its tags stay `owner = "priya.nair"` and `cost_center = "CC-4410"`, plus
`env = "dev"`. Every resource of the lake gets the same three tags.
- **The storage account is our data lake**: ADLS Gen2 (hierarchical namespace), zone-redundant (ZRS), TLS 1.2
at least, and no anonymous blob access (`allow_nested_items_to_be_public = false`).
- **One container per zone**: `bronze`, `silver` and `gold`, from a variable `zones` (a `set(string)`), with a
single `azurerm_storage_container.zone` block. Next quarter we add `platinum` by editing the variable only.
- An output `dfs_endpoint` with the account's DFS endpoint, for the pipeline team.
Keep the names we use in the other repos: `azurerm_resource_group.lake`, `azurerm_storage_account.lake`.
When you're done, `terraform plan` must say there is nothing left to change.
This is the lab's simulated subscription: nothing is created in Azure.

acceptance.text: The portal-created resource group is managed by Terraform (imported, not recreated), with the three tags.

hints: Start with `terraform init`, then `terraform plan`, and read the plan before any apply. `az group show -n rg-saleslake-dev` gives the resource group's id.

A resource that already exists must be imported before Terraform manages it: `terraform import azurerm_resource_group.lake <id>`, or an `import { to = ..., id = ... }` block that the next plan shows as "will be imported".
After an import, the plan compares the portal's tags with yours: tags missing from the configuration would be removed. A `locals { tags = {...} }` map avoids repeating them.
`is_hns_enabled` cannot be changed on an existing account (the plan says "forces replacement"). Here the account does not exist yet, so set it before the first apply.
`for_each` takes a map or a set of strings: `type = set(string)` on the variable, `each.key` for the name, `storage_account_id = azurerm_storage_account.lake.id`.
